hints.title: Allowed Prime Factor Reduction Obstacle
hints.text: An ugly number is a positive integer whose prime factors are limited to 2, 3, and 5. What remains if you strip away all occurrences of these allowed factors?

hints.title: Full Prime Stripping Invariant
hints.text: Repeatedly dividing by each allowed prime factor until indivisible must leave exactly 1 for the number to be considered ugly.

hints.title: Factor Division Loop Procedure
hints.text: If n is less than or equal to zero, return false immediately. While n is divisible by 2, divide by 2. Repeat for factors 3 and 5. Return true if remaining value equals 1, otherwise false.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input element count or target integer bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Factoring numbers completely via trial division takes unnecessary time when only three prime factors are allowed.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Directly dividing out 2, 3, and 5 runs in O(log N) iterations with O(1) extra space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate must reject non-positive inputs (n <= 0) and verify that stripping 2, 3, and 5 reduces the number to 1.
